title: 'The bot created the savings. The people created the new revenue' — James Brake reads IKEA's refusal to cut 8,500 jobs through Incorruptible
summary: Ingka Group, which runs most IKEA stores, rolled out its Billie chatbot in 2021 and saw it resolve about 47% of inquiries. Brake's point is what IKEA did next: it retrained the 8,500 call-centre workers rather than cutting them, moving some to remote interior-design consulting, a channel he reports is now IKEA's fastest-growing. He credits the lens explicitly to the themes in Incorruptible, and IKEA is one of the companies Eric names from the stage as structurally unusual. The argument is the book's own — that the short-term-efficient move and the long-term-valuable one diverge, and structure decides which a company takes.
blockquote: In an era where “AI replaced X employees” is treated as a victory metric, IKEA's decision looks less like sentiment and more like long-term strategy. Retraining loyal, hard-working people who already understood the customer turned out to be one of the bigger wins of the whole effort.
